knowledge:
- key_parameters: argc=Integer specifying the number of arguments in argv ;; argv=Character vector of command-line style arguments (e.g., "-c" for color path, "-d" for data path, "-o" for output path, "-f" for format, "-s" for scale) ;; format=Format of the input file, specified via "-f" in argv as either "CHROMDRAW" (default) or "bed"
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use when visualizing chromosome structures (linear karyotypes) or comparing multiple karyotypes against each other (circular karyotypes) with cytogenetic marks like rDNA loci.
- pitfalls: The first element of the argv vector in chromDraw must always be the package name "chromDraw" ;; When defining a centromere in GenomicRanges, the name must be set to "CENTROMERE" and the ranges must be [0,0] ;; BED files must contain at least the first nine fields per record ;; In the custom text input format, centromere definitions must immediately follow the block that is directly before the centromere.

workflows.name: text_file_karyotype
workflows.intent: Visualize karyotypes and cytogenetic marks using custom text-based definition and color files.
input: karyotype_definition.txt (plain text file containing karyotype, chromosome, block, centromere, and mark definitions)
color_definitions.txt (plain text file containing color names and RGB values)
workflows.stages: 1. Define output path and input file paths ;; 2. Run visualization using chromDraw with command-line style arguments

workflows.name: genomic_ranges_karyotype
workflows.intent: Visualize karyotypes and cytogenetic marks directly from R using GenomicRanges and a color data frame.
input: genomic_ranges_object (GRanges object containing chromosome, block, centromere, and color metadata)
color_dataframe (data.frame containing color names and RGB values)
workflows.stages: 1. Create or load GenomicRanges object with karyotype structure ;; 2. Create or load data frame with color definitions ;; 3. Run visualization using chromDrawGR

workflows.name: bed_file_karyotype
workflows.intent: Visualize karyotypes from a BED format file.
input: bed_file.bed (BED file containing at least the first nine fields per record)
workflows.stages: 1. Define output path and BED input file path ;; 2. Run visualization using chromDraw specifying the BED format
